- Summary of asks: PayGrid wants a secure, auditable authentication model for Redwood API usage (embeddings + reranker + tool-calls) with clear rotation & minimal ops friction. You also flagged Okta SSO for admin access and SOC 2 evidence for procurement.

- Recommended approach (POC -> production):

  2) Prod: recommended pattern is OAuth2 Client Credentials / JWT service account flow (private key + token exchange) with automated private-key rotation or short-lived signing keys via your KMS.

I attached a short SDK quickstart (redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf) that shows server-side examples (Node/Python) for exchanging a JWT for an access token and calling the embeddings endpoint. Also attached a suggested rotation cadence (redwood-rotation-schedule.csv) for review.

- Do you want Redwood to host the rotation orchestration (we push rotated keys into your KMS) or do you prefer PayGrid to run rotation and call a Redwood token endpoint?
- Who will own the Okta integration (IDP team contact)?
- Any specific retention/PII constraints for audit logs?

Proposed next steps:
- Tech deep-dive on Wed 12/08 11:00–12:00 PT (Ben to lead auth flow + token exchange demo; Marissa will demo a reranker/embeddings sample).
- We’ll provide a short-lived token demo and a sample rotation schedule before the meeting.

If that all looks good I’ll send an invite and attach links.

Thanks for the details, Priya. A few technical clarifications and one proposed path forward: 

- POC path (fast): a single server-side API key stored in your vault with rotation every 7–14 days. This gets you up quickly and lets Marissa validate reranker examples with real traffic.

- Production path (recommended): JWT service account with private key kept in your KMS. Flow we typically recommend:
  * Create a service account in PayGrid with an associated JSON that contains the public key/metadata only.
  * PayGrid holds the private key in Okta/KMS and issues signed JWTs.
  * Redwood exposes a token-exchange endpoint (OAuth2 token endpoint) that accepts the signed JWT and returns a short-lived access token (TTL 15m–1h) scoped to the model/route.
  * Token introspection or audit hooks will emit token-id, service-account-id, request-route, model-id for your logs.

- Rotation schedule suggestion (attached in CSV):
  * Private key rotation (KMS): rotate every 90 days, maintain last 2 keys for rollover.
  * Access token TTL: 15 minutes (recommended) for high-volume endpoints; 1 hour acceptable for batch jobs.
  * If you want zero-key-management, we can enable Redwood-managed signing keys that integrate with your Okta as a federation trust; this reduces your operational burden but changes the trust model (we can provide an SLA addendum).

On structured outputs & tool calling: the SDK examples include a structured output schema (JSON Schema) and tool-call hooks. Marissa will show a demo that wires embeddings -> dense reranker -> tool-call in a single flow (we do deterministic post-processing so you can reproducibly rerank).

I’ll prep the rotation CSV and a sample token-exchange curl snippet for Wed.

—Ben
